extracted.intended_audience: scientific researchers and research administrators seeking American Heart Association funding (including prospective AHA professional members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and organizational standards for applicants and stakeholders engaging with the American Heart Association's research funding programs, including program eligibility, review expectations, and application resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 Essential Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: At our core are 12 Essential Elements that guide the organization's research vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references these as the foundational elements directing AHA research priorities and decisions; the specific elements are not listed on this page but are described as shaping the organization's research vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with mission (timely, mission-related programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding programs are described as timely, mission-related programs that are continually added to address priority scientific areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect funding opportunities to prioritize topics closely aligned with the AHA mission and strategic priorities; proposals that address mission-key areas are more likely to be competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review by volunteer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by peer volunteers (the page notes 2,800 reviewers evaluated 5,242 proposals in 2024-25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will undergo peer review by a large volunteer reviewer pool; applicants should prepare proposals for critical scientific evaluation by peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success rate metric (percent funded of full proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Success rates are defined as the percent funded of the total number of full proposals submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cautions that reported success rates should not be used to predict future program performance; success rates are a descriptive metric of past funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid Impact Research Award selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rapid Impact Research Award is reserved for research considered urgent, high-priority and capable of delivering critical results to patients quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This award targets projects with high urgency and clear, near-term potential for patient impact—applicants should demonstrate urgency, priority, and capacity for rapid translation/delivery of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategically Focused Research Networks / multidisciplinary collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2014 the AHA has funded multi-disciplinary teams (strategic networks) that collaborate on specific areas of science that are key to the mission; summaries report on the work at the conclusion of each grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding for strategic networks prioritizes multidisciplinary collaboration on mission-relevant topics, with expectations for deliverables and reporting at grant conclusion; teams should plan collaborative structure and end-of-grant summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of application resources and compliance with application instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The AHA provides tips and tools for preparing and submitting proposals, including step-by-step application instructions, live webinars, videos, fact sheets, and helpful websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to follow the provided application instructions and use available resources to ensure compliant, complete submissions; failure to follow instructions may affect review or eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional membership access to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Becoming an AHA Professional Member provides access to apply for research funding awards and other benefits (e.g., journal access, council affiliation, discounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some application privileges or eligibility pathways may be tied to professional membership status; prospective applicants should verify membership requirements for specific funding opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific eligibility (example: SURE Scholars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs like the SURE Scholars Program are targeted (e.g., a unique summer research program for underrepresented college students interested in STEM careers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review program-specific eligibility criteria—some AHA programs are targeted to specific populations, career stages, or institution types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data submission and performance tracking requirement (Get With The Guidelines®)
rubrics_metrics.description: Get With The Guidelines® is a hospital-based quality improvement program designed to close treatment gaps; it requires meeting data submission requirements while tracking and reporting hospital performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals participating in this program must submit required data and use the provided modules (coronary artery disease, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, stroke, resuscitation) and materials based on evidence-based guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and tracking via reSEARCH@heart portal
rubrics_metrics.description: The reSEARCH@heart portal provides current data on investigators, institutions, awards and resulting publications funded by the AHA since 2001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and administrators can use the portal to review historical funding patterns, investigator/institution award records, and publication outcomes to inform applications and institutional strategy.
